item.statement_excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix a compact smooth Riemannian manifold $(X,g)$ and a period $T>0$. Consider smooth families $J(\sigma,\tau,x)^2=-I$ on cylinders $[a,b]\times(\mathbb R/T\mathbb Z)$, with uniform bounds for $J$ and its first two target covariant derivatives. There are constants $\varepsilon,c,C>0$ depending only on these data such that the following holds. If
$$u_\sigma+J(\sigma,\tau,u)u_\tau=0,\qquad \sup|du|_g+\sup(|\partial_\sigma J|+|\partial_\tau J|)\le\varepsilon,$$
then a fixed smooth embedding $F:X\to\mathbb R^N$ can be chosen once for the target so that, for $V=F\circ u$ and $e(\sigma)=\tfrac12\int_0^T|V_\tau|^2d\tau$,
$$e''\ge c^2 e,\qquad e(\sigma)\le e(a)e^{-c(\sigma-a)}+e(b)e^{-c(b-\sigma)}.$$
Consequently, for $0\le R\le(b-a)/2$,
$$E_g\bigl(u;[a+R,b-R]\times S_T^1\bigr)\le C(e(a)+e(b))e^{-cR}.$$
Here $E_g=\tfrac12\int|du|_g^2$. The energy density at either endpoint is bounded by $CT\varepsilon^2$. Thus central neck energies tend to zero as $R\to\infty$, uniformly in neck length, for maps satisfying these hypotheses. This statement concerns closed cylinders, not boundary necks.

proof_step_donor_fragments.exact_current_text: Choose a finite chart cover and smooth subordinate functions $\phi_i$ with compact supports in those charts and sum one, obtained by Euclidean bumps and normalization. The map $F(x)=(\phi_i(x),\phi_i(x)x_i(x))_i$ is a smooth embedding: at an index where $\phi_i>0$, equality of the displayed coordinates recovers the original chart point, and vanishing of all their derivatives recovers a zero tangent vector. Compactness makes it a homeomorphism onto its image and makes its differential uniformly comparable with the metric $g$. Its first and second covariant derivatives have uniform bounds. This fixes $F$ independently of the cylinder and its map. [given, construct, algebra]

Let $H=\Delta V$, taking the ordinary flat source Laplacian componentwise. The composition rule and [F1] give $$H=dF(
abla_\sigma u_\sigma+
abla_	au u_	au)+(
abla dF)(u_\sigma,u_\sigma)+(
abla dF)(u_	au,u_	au).$$ Uniform coefficient and embedding bounds therefore give $|H|\le C_0(|du|_g+\kappa)|du|_g$. The original equation and the bound for $J$ give $|du|_g\le C_1|u_	au|_g\le C_2|V_	au|$. After imposing the stated smallness, $$|H|\le C_3\varepsilon|V_	au|.$$ This is a pointwise estimate on actual maps into $X$; no ambient extension of $J$ or model moduli equation is assumed. [F1, step 1.1, given, algebra]

Put $w=V_\tau$. It has zero angular mean because $V$ is periodic, and $\Delta w=\partial_\tau H$ because derivatives of a smooth Euclidean map commute. Twice differentiating $e=\tfrac12\int|w|^2$ and integrating by parts only in the periodic angular direction gives $$e''=\int_0^T\bigl(|w_\sigma|^2+|w_\tau|^2-\langle w_\tau,H\rangle\bigr)d\tau.$$ There are no endpoint terms in this integration. By step 2.1 and Young's inequality this is at least $$\int_0^T|w_\sigma|^2+\tfrac12|w_\tau|^2-\tfrac12 C_3^2\varepsilon^2|w|^2\,d\tau.$$ Let $\lambda=(2\pi/T)^2$ and choose $\varepsilon>0$ so that $C_3^2\varepsilon^2\le\lambda/2$. Then [F2] gives $e''\ge(\lambda/4)\int|w|^2=(\lambda/2)e$. Set $c=\sqrt{\lambda/2}$. [F2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

Let $h(\sigma)=e(a)e^{-c(\sigma-a)}+e(b)e^{-c(b-\sigma)}$. It satisfies $h''-c^2h=0$ and dominates $e$ at both endpoints. If $e-h$ had a positive value, it would have a positive interior maximum; there its second derivative is nonpositive, contrary to $(e-h)''\ge c^2(e-h)>0$. Thus $e\le h$ throughout the cylinder, giving the claimed pointwise exponential bound. The argument also covers vanishing endpoint values, since $e$ is nonnegative and smooth. [step 3.1, construct, algebra]

The equation and uniform metric comparability give $$E_g(u;[a+R,b-R]\times S_T^1)\le C_4\int_{a+R}^{b-R}e(\sigma)d\sigma.$$ Integrating the two exponentials from step 4.1 bounds the last integral by $c^{-1}(e(a)+e(b))e^{-cR}$. Finally $|V_\tau|\le C|u_\tau|_g\le C\varepsilon$, so $e(a)+e(b)\le CT\varepsilon^2$. This proves all assertions, including uniform decay of central neck energy. A boundary neck has angular endpoint terms and is not covered by the periodic argument. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎
